source.title: Grokking as an entanglement transition in tensor network machine learning
source.authors: Domenico Pomarico; A. Monaco; Giuseppe Magnifico; A. Lacalamita; E. Pantaleo; L. Bellantuono; S. Tangaro; T. Maggipinto; M. La Rocca; E. Picardi; N. Amoroso; G. Pesole; S. Stramaglia; R. Bellotti

record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking-like delayed generalization in new, non-algorithmic settings: MPS classifiers on Fashion-MNIST image subsets and hepatocellular-carcinoma gene-expression communities.
record.gate_note: Reports training and independent-set classification dynamics, including grokking transitions, for Fashion-MNIST binary tasks and gene communities. The fake-sneaker-versus-sneaker experiment is described as a contrasting control, but the text does not report an independent-set generalization result for it. The entanglement and magnetization measurements do not test the specific gradual-circuit, memorization-removal, and anticipation account in V2.
record.test_reason: The study trains MPS tensor-network classifiers on non-algorithmic data (6×6 Fashion-MNIST, HCC gene expression) and reports independent-set generalization dynamics it calls grokking. This bears on the non-algorithmic-data part of V3. Only the dress-vs-sneaker case states that test metrics jump after a training-set overfitting regime.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim to numerically show that MPS grokking relates to an entanglement transition from volume-law to sub-volume-law. In the gene data the transition occurs in every community, but effective grokking occurs only in about 60%, so grokking implies the transition but not the converse. They also use MPS correlations to find enriched gene sub-communities.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient-trained MPS classifiers on Fashion-MNIST and gene-expression communities, rather than small algorithmic datasets and the original neural-network setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Fashion-MNIST transition sweep varies with the random initialization and image subsample. In gene communities, transition sweeps and performance differ by community; gene-expression feature ordering affects entropy behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokking in MPS coincides with a volume-to-sub-volume entanglement-entropy transition. Every gene community shows the entanglement transition, but only about 60% generalize.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking in tensor-network classifiers coincides with an entanglement transition that is necessary but not sufficient for generalization.

record.code_released: Available from the authors upon reasonable request; no URL stated.
record.problems: The Fashion-MNIST results use 1% subsamples and 6 × 6 compressed images. Exact values for most task-level results are presented in figures, and no uncertainty estimates are stated. Gene-community generalization is reported in almost 60% of cases, not uniformly.
record.rows_left_out: No additional task rows omitted. The fake-sneaker-versus-sneaker contrast is mentioned in gate_note; the text describes its mask and coherence behavior but does not report a relevant independent-set generalization result.

untested.parts: Switching the delay on or off via initialization scale or weight norm (lazy-to-rich); text and molecule data.
No algorithmic datasets; no variation of training-set size.
No circuit analysis, no memorization-removal test, no test of whether progress measures anticipate the jump.
No weight decay, no critical dataset size, no ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms across runs.

missing.what: Per-community independent-set accuracy, sensitivity and specificity after the magnetization transition; 12 communities exceed 0.65 accuracy.
Accuracy ranking of the Fashion-MNIST sneaker classifications (Fig. 7 legend).

record.verdict_notes: The study's notion of grokking is loose. Outside dress-vs-sneaker, it is defined by magnetization or entanglement transitions, or by gain over a random classifier, rather than by test accuracy rising long after training saturation. Hence most Fashion-MNIST rows are cannot_determine. Training uses MSE loss with sweep-based gradient descent and norm rescaling; uncertainty and multiple seeds are not reported. The fake-sneaker control reports no generalization metric.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic dataset or modular-arithmetic task is tested.

The study measures magnetization and entanglement dynamics, but does not test gradual formation of an identifiable generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, or whether continuous progress measures anticipate the test-accuracy jump.
Tests grokking-like behavior on image and gene-expression data, but does not vary initialization scale or weight norm to switch the behavior on or off; it does not test text or molecule datasets.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic large-model data.
Does not test weight decay or another low-norm bias, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
Does not identify and compare algorithms learned across runs.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities, floating-point softmax limits, or whether controlling these removes grokking.

rows.measure: Effective grokking in independent-set classification relative to a random classifier

source_check.correct: Across Table 1 communities, feature counts range from 23 to 48. Bond dimension is 400 except C12, C28, C29 and C41: 1000; C23: 300; C24: 100. Almost 60% achieve sufficient independent-set performance gain over random classification. This criterion does not establish delayed generalization; V3 state: cannot_determine.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Restrict this verdict to C29: r11 explicitly places generalization gain at approximately the same sweep as maximal training accuracy, showing the delay absent. For the remaining communities, r10's almost-60% performance-gain criterion does not establish whether a delay occurs and cannot support a group-wide limits_scope verdict.
